title: About
note: PLACEHOLDER COPY — dev-team stand-ins. The Aizu Momen facts that are load-bearing (120 years, two remaining factories) came from discovery; everything phrased as narrative is a placeholder for Noi.

seo.description: The Yammaman story — Aizu cotton, a 120-year-old mill, and a brand built around made-to-order cloth.

props.heading: Two factories left
props.subheading: Aizu Momen has been woven in Fukushima since the Meiji era. Almost none of it is left.

props.heading: Why this cloth
body: Aizu Momen is a cotton woven with a technique brought to Fukushima in the nineteenth century. It is dense, it holds dye unevenly on purpose, and it softens rather than wears out.
The count of surviving mills is the reason Yammaman exists. A craft with two practitioners is a craft that ends within one working life unless someone buys the cloth.

props.heading: The mill has its own site
props.body: HARAPPA is the factory itself — its history, its process, and the fabrics it can still weave.
